## Who Counts as Unemployed?

The unemployment rate is calculated using the number of unemployed people and the number of employed people—not everyone who does not have a job. To be counted as unemployed, a person generally must not have been employed during the reference week, have been available for work (with an exception for temporary illness), and have actively looked for work during the four-week period ending with that week.

There is an exception to the active-search requirement for someone on temporary layoff who expects to be recalled. If that person meets the other conditions, they may count as unemployed without searching for work during the four-week period.

By contrast, someone whose only job-search activity was browsing job listings has not met the active-search requirement. Availability and the specified survey periods matter too. These conditions determine whether someone is counted as unemployed—and included, along with employed people, in the rate’s denominator.
